evidence: Routes 3 (published totals) + 6 (keying polarity) + 2 (structural signature of the R markers), computed on live irw_fetch data, n=189 complete cases, re-runnable as verify_pierro_2018_locomotion_s4.R. The claim tested is that loc1..loc12 (with locR6, locR9) are the RMQ Locomotion items in the scoring key's own order (Q1,Q3,Q4,Q5,Q8,Q13,Q16,Q21,Q24,Q25,Q28,Q29), whose two reverse-worded items fall at within-subscale positions 6 and 9. (a) Storage direction and scale identity: as stored, alpha = 0.8320 vs the paper's published Study 4 .83, M = 4.3743 vs 4.37, SD = 0.6192 vs .62; un-recoding locR6/locR9 gives 0.6669 / 4.2218 / 0.4839 and misses all three; the S4 .sav's own 'locomotion' composite equals the plain unrecoded mean of the 12 columns to max |diff| 0.0 over 189 cases (0.8333 against the recoded mean). r(locomotion, assessment) from the live sibling tables = -0.0463 against the published -.05. So the values are already reverse-recoded, which is what the flipped anchors on locR6/locR9 encode -- and this is NOT inherited: pierro_2018_locomotion_s3 stores the same instrument raw. (b) Which positions are reverse-worded: after un-recoding, corrected item-rest r is locR6 -0.256 and locR9 -0.403 -- the only two negatives -- against +0.341 (loc1) to +0.590 (loc12) for the other ten, exactly the pair the RMQ key predicts. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: nothing separates the ten positively-worded items from one another (alpha is permutation-invariant and item-rest pins a polarity class, not an order within it), and nothing says which of Q13/Q24 is locR6 vs locR9. The only non-statistical tie to a specific position is content: the paper's single quoted locomotion item is canonical Q21 = position 8 = loc8, which is what ships. Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED.

evidence: Route 3 (published subscale statistics + the published correlation row), Pierro et al. 2018 Table 4, N=189, all computed from the LIVE IRW table. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: the four codes are the PRESENT subscale, stored raw. Live composite M 5.115, SD 1.001, Cronbach alpha 0.854 against the published Present row 5.12 / 1.00 / .85 -- L1 distance 0.010, versus 0.160 for the published Past row (5.10/1.09/.91) and 0.540 for the Future row (5.54/1.05/.92). The live composite also reproduces Table 4's entire Present correlation row: locomotion .251 vs published .25, assessment .003 vs .003, past -.094 vs -.09, future .331 vs .33 (largest deviation .004); the Past row would read -.12/.41 and the Future row .37/.02, so the block is not confusable. Live composite equals the deposit's own 'present' column at r = 1.0000 with max|diff| 0.000 over 189 persons, so the items are unreversed. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: which of TFpresent1, TFpresent2, TFpresent3, TFpresent4 carries which sentence. Every number above is permutation-invariant across the four codes -- any reordering of the four shipped wordings passes identically. Zero of the four items are distinguished from any other. The .sav has no variable labels, this study publishes no per-item statistics, all four items share the 1-7 range and the same polarity, and the two cross-sample attempts against the Italian validation (PMC7851924, N=1458) DISAGREE by one adjacent swap each: live item-total correlations .511/.788/.753/.748 match the Italian current-focus loading ranks (.672 < .704 < .751) under the shipped order, while live means 5.661/4.937/5.011/4.852 match the Italian mean ranks (5.43 > 5.25 > 4.66) only under the rival order. Hence NO_ROUTE for the item<->text axis. The shipped order is the instrument's own ascending Shipp numbering for the three items whose Shipp number is recoverable (2, 4, 8) with the unrecoverable one ('I think about where I am today', Shipp 5 or 10) placed last; that is an inference, not a checked fact.

Exempt by DERIVATION, not merely by basis. data/wesselmann_2018_ostracism_veterans.py melts the PLOS S1 .sav on the literal column list [f'drri{i}' for i in range(1,13)] (var_name='item'), so the IRW item code IS the source column name (pattern 1: no rename, no positional assignment): 12/12 live item codes present verbatim in the .sav header, 12/12 carrying their own SPSS variable label (label lengths 32-111 chars, all far under the 255 truncation cap), and item_text equals those labels with 12/12 exact string equality, checked programmatically. Corroborated independently by the authors' OSF codebook (sha256 b3e1ee71...8a9c), which lists the same 12 codes against the same 12 sentences, and by the DRRI-2 Scales form (sha256 5b17c1bf...080e), whose Section G is exactly 12 items in the same order (11/12 character-identical; drri2 differs only by a dropped sentence-final period). No positional step exists that could permute text across codes. The resp AXIS did carry inference (the .sav has 0 value-label sets and the study's codebook misprints anchor 1) and was checked numerically, N=128: the file's own 'concern' composite equals the plain unreversed mean of drri1..drri12 with max |diff| = 0.000, against max |diff| = 4.000 for the reversed mean, so nothing is stored reverse-coded; that composite correlates +0.403 traitanx, +0.394 stateanx, +0.393 ptsd, +0.260 distress, -0.179 support and -0.277 milsupport, so high raw = more deployment concern, fixing 1 = 'Strongly disagree' and 5 = 'Strongly agree'. Raw-item alpha 0.902 (n=117 complete) reproduces the paper's reported .90. What this does NOT establish: nothing tests the three interior anchors 'Somewhat disagree' / 'Neither agree nor disagree' / 'Somewhat agree' individually -- they are the DRRI-2 form's printed labels for 2/3/4, carried over because the .sav has no value labels; only the endpoints and the monotone direction are checked against data.
